proofs.proof_tex:
For a response type \(r=(X_0,X_1,V,W)\), define its factual arm-\(z\) cell by
\[
 F_z(r)=(X_z,Y_z^F),\qquad
 Y_z^F=\begin{cases}V_{X_z},&X_z\in T,\\ W_{X_z z},&X_z\in U.\end{cases}
\]
If \(q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)\), put
\[
 \pi_{ij}=\Pr_q\{F_0(R)=i,F_1(R)=j\},\qquad i,j\in\mathcal I.
\]
Random assignment, \(Z\perp R\), and the mixed-trust observation map imply
\[
 \sum_j\pi_{ij}=\Pr_q\{F_0(R)=i\}=p_i^0,\qquad
 \sum_i\pi_{ij}=\Pr_q\{F_1(R)=j\}=p_j^1.
\]
If \(i=(x,y)\), \(j=(x,y')\), and \(x\in T\), then both factual outcomes equal the single bit \(V_x\).  Hence \(\pi_{ij}=0\) when \(y\ne y'\), and therefore \(\pi\in\Pi_T(p)\).

Conversely, fix \(\pi\in\Pi_T(p)\).  For every allowed edge \(i=((x_0,y_0))\), \(j=((x_1,y_1))\), construct a response type \(r_{ij}\) by setting \(X_0=x_0\) and \(X_1=x_1\).  If \(x_z\in T\), set \(V_{x_z}=y_z\).  These prescriptions cannot conflict: a conflict would require \(x_0=x_1\in T\) and \(y_0\ne y_1\), which is a forbidden edge.  Complete all unprescribed trusted bits arbitrarily.  If \(x_z\in U\), set \(W_{x_z z}=y_z\), and complete the other unprescribed \(W\)-bits arbitrarily.  Let \(q\) be the push-forward of the finite mass function \(\pi\) under \((i,j)\mapsto r_{ij}\), combining masses if two completed edges give the same type.  Then
\[
 \Pr_q(X_z=x,V_x=y)=p^z_{xy}\quad(x\in T),\qquad
 \Pr_q(X_z=x,W_{xz}=y)=p^z_{xy}\quad(x\in U),
\]
so \(q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)\).  This proves the two-way transport reduction by an explicit finite edgewise lift.

It remains to optimize the target within a fixed edge.  Write
\[
 A(i,j)=\mathbf 1\{i=s\text{ or }j=s\},\qquad
 B(i,j)=\mathbf 1\{i=t\text{ or }j=t\}.
\]
For every completion of an allowed edge, factual consistency gives
\[
 V_a\le 1-A(i,j),\qquad V_b\ge B(i,j).
\]
Indeed, \(A=1\) forces \(V_a=0\), whereas \(A=0\) only gives the binary bound \(V_a\le1\); similarly, \(B=1\) forces \(V_b=1\), whereas \(B=0\) gives \(V_b\ge0\).  Thus
\[
 V_b-V_a\ge -1+A(i,j)+B(i,j)=d^-(i,j).
\]
Equality is attainable edge by edge: set \(V_a=1-A(i,j)\) and \(V_b=B(i,j)\), which agrees with any factual observation of \(a\) or \(b\), and complete every other bit as above.  Consequently, for each fixed \(\pi\), the smallest target value among its lifts is \(\sum_{ij}\pi_{ij}d^-(i,j)\).  Inclusion--exclusion and the margins yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_{ij}\pi_{ij}A(i,j)&=p_s^0+p_s^1-\pi_{ss}=\alpha_0+\alpha_1-\pi_{ss},\\
 \sum_{ij}\pi_{ij}B(i,j)&=p_t^0+p_t^1-\pi_{tt}=\beta_0+\beta_1-\pi_{tt}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(\sum_{ij}\pi_{ij}=1\), it follows that
\[
 \sum_{ij}\pi_{ij}d^-(i,j)
 =-1+\alpha_0+\alpha_1+\beta_0+\beta_1-\pi_{ss}-\pi_{tt}
 =\kappa-\pi_{ss}-\pi_{tt}.
\]
Taking the infimum over response laws and the supremum over their equivalent couplings proves
\[
 \inf_{q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)}\theta_{ab}(q)
 =\kappa-\sup_{\pi\in\Pi_T(p)}(\pi_{ss}+\pi_{tt}).
\]
The equality is an equality of finite attained optima whenever the compatible class is nonempty; with the standard extended-real conventions it also remains formally valid when both classes are empty.

Write \(r_i=p_i^0\) and \(c_j=p_j^1\).  Because \(p^0\) and \(p^1\) are probability vectors, \(r_i,c_j\ge0\) and both totals are one.  For a restricted row \(i=(x,y)\), \(x\in T\), let its unique forbidden partner be \(f(i)=(x,1-y)\).  If a coupling exists, then its forbidden entry is zero and
\[
 r_i+c_{f(i)}
 =\sum_j\pi_{ij}+\sum_k\pi_{k f(i)}\le \sum_{k,j}\pi_{kj}=1.
\]
This is exactly \(p^0_{xy}+p^1_{x,1-y}\le1\), proving necessity.

We now prove sufficiency without a positivity or interior argument.  For a row set \(A\), let \(N(A)\) be its set of allowed neighboring columns.  If \(|A|\ge2\), then \(N(A)\) is the whole column set: any column is forbidden to at most one row, because the forbidden edges form a matching.  Hence \(r(A)\le1=c(N(A))\).  If \(A=\{i\}\) and \(i\) is restricted, then \(N(A)\) contains every column except \(f(i)\), and
\[
 r(A)\le 1-c_{f(i)}=c(N(A))
\]
is precisely the displayed compatibility inequality.  If \(i\) is unrestricted, \(N(\{i\})\) is the whole column set and \(r_i\le1\).  Thus
\[
 r(A)\le c(N(A))\qquad\text{for every row set }A. \tag{1}
\]

For completeness, consider all nonnegative partial flows on allowed edges with row sums at most \(r_i\) and column sums at most \(c_j\).  This is a nonempty compact finite-dimensional set, so a partial flow \(\pi^\star\) maximizing transported mass exists.  Suppose its mass \(F\) were less than one.  Start from every row with unused supply and follow alternating paths that use an allowed row-to-column edge forward and a positive-flow edge backward.  If a reachable column had unused demand, increasing the forward edges and decreasing the backward edges by the positive bottleneck amount would increase \(F\), a contradiction.  Hence every reachable column is saturated.  Let \(A\) and \(B\) be the reachable rows and columns.  Every allowed neighbor of a reachable row is reachable, so \(B=N(A)\).  Every positive-flow edge entering \(B\) comes from \(A\), because its reverse edge makes its row reachable.  Therefore
\[
 c(B)=\sum_{j\in B}\sum_i\pi^\star_{ij}
       =\sum_{i\in A}\sum_j\pi^\star_{ij}<r(A),
\]
where the strict inequality holds because \(A\) contains a starting row with unused supply.  This contradicts (1).  Hence \(F=1\), and \(\pi^\star\in\Pi_T(p)\).  This alternating-path proof also gives finite augmentation: choose a shortest augmenting path at each step and augment by its bottleneck.  Residual source distances never decrease; if a directed edge becomes a bottleneck again after being restored, its tail distance has increased by at least two.  There are finitely many vertices and directed edges, so only finitely many such bottlenecks, and the procedure terminates.  No strict margin condition is used.

Now reserve \(r_s\ge0\) on \((s,s)\) and \(r_t\ge0\) on \((t,t)\).  The residual row and column margins have common total
\[
 Q=1-r_s-r_t.
\]
Their nonnegativity is equivalent, on the affected cells, to
\[
 r_s\le\alpha_0,\quad r_s\le\alpha_1,\qquad
 r_t\le\beta_0,\quad r_t\le\beta_1. \tag{2}
\]
Apply the just-proved criterion with total \(Q\): a restricted residual row \(i\) must satisfy \(r_i'+c_{f(i)}'\le Q\).  For category \(a\), its two inequalities are
\[
 (\alpha_0-r_s)+\gamma_1\le1-r_s-r_t,\qquad
 \gamma_0+(\alpha_1-r_s)\le1-r_s-r_t,
\]
or equivalently
\[
 r_t\le1-\alpha_0-\gamma_1,\qquad
 r_t\le1-\gamma_0-\alpha_1. \tag{3}
\]
For category \(b\), they are
\[
 (\beta_0-r_t)+\delta_1\le1-r_s-r_t,\qquad
 \delta_0+(\beta_1-r_t)\le1-r_s-r_t,
\]
or equivalently
\[
 r_s\le1-\beta_0-\delta_1,\qquad
 r_s\le1-\delta_0-\beta_1. \tag{4}
\]
For \(c\in T\setminus\{a,b\}\), no cell margin was changed, and the two inequalities are
\[
 p^0_{cy}+p^1_{c,1-y}\le1-r_s-r_t
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad r_s+r_t\le h_{cy},\qquad y\in\{0,1\}. \tag{5}
\]
There is no inequality for an untrusted row.  Combining (2)--(5) gives exactly
\[
 0\le r_s\le u,\qquad 0\le r_t\le v,\qquad
 r_s+r_t\le h_{cy}\quad(c\in T\setminus\{a,b\},\ y\in\{0,1\}). \tag{6}
\]
These conditions also imply \(Q\ge0\), because \(r_s+r_t\le u+v\le\alpha_0+\beta_0\le1\).  Conversely, (6) gives nonnegative residual margins and every residual compatibility inequality, so the alternating-path construction completes them.  If \(Q=0\), all residual margins are zero and the zero residual flow is the required completion.  Thus the equivalence includes zero cells, equality cuts, and every other boundary stratum.

The observable law \(P\) is a probability vector on the \(4|\mathcal E|\) cells \((z,x,y)\in\{0,1\}\times\mathcal E\times\{0,1\}\), hence has dimension \(4|\mathcal E|-1\).  Under \(0<\rho<1\), it is equivalently parameterized by the scalar \(\rho\) and the two \((2|\mathcal E|-1)\)-dimensional conditional vectors \(p^0,p^1\), through
\[
 \Pr_P(Z=z,X=x,Y=y)=\rho^z(1-\rho)^{1-z}p^z_{xy}.
\]
The unobserved parameter is a mass function \(q\) on the finite set \(\mathcal R_T\), and the scalar causal target is \(\theta_{ab}(q)=\mathbb E_q[V_b-V_a]\).  Thus the identified set, rather than an observed-law definition of the target, is
\[
 \Theta_I(P)=\{\theta_{ab}(q):q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)\}.
\]
Model compatibility makes this set nonempty.  It is compact and convex because \(\mathcal Q_T(p)\) is a nonempty closed convex subset of a finite simplex and \(\theta_{ab}\) is linear.

By the transport-completion lemma, its lower endpoint equals \(\kappa\) minus the greatest feasible value of \(r_s+r_t=\pi_{ss}+\pi_{tt}\).  Compatibility implies that \(u,v,h_{cy}\) are nonnegative.  The residual-cap lemma shows that every feasible pair obeys
\[
 r_s+r_t\le u+v,\qquad r_s+r_t\le h_{cy}\quad(c\in T\setminus\{a,b\},\ y\in\{0,1\}),
\]
and hence \(r_s+r_t\le D_T(p)\).  Conversely, set
\[
 r_s=\min\{u,D_T(p)\},\qquad r_t=D_T(p)-r_s.
\]
Then \(r_s,r_t\ge0\).  If \(D_T(p)\le u\), then \(r_t=0\); if \(D_T(p)>u\), then \(r_t=D_T(p)-u\le v\), because \(D_T(p)\le u+v\).  Also \(r_s\le u\) and \(r_s+r_t=D_T(p)\le h_{cy}\) for every trusted nuisance cell.  The residual-cap lemma therefore supplies a coupling after the reserved diagonals are inserted.  Any additional residual mass on either selected diagonal would make the total exceed \(D_T(p)\), contradicting the already-proved necessary caps; thus the completed coupling has
\[
 \pi_{ss}+\pi_{tt}=D_T(p).
\]
The edgewise minimizing completion in the transport lemma is exactly the prescribed construction of \(q_T^-(p)\).  It is a finite law in \(\mathcal Q_T(p)\), and
\[
 \theta_{ab}(q_T^-(p))=\kappa-D_T(p)=L_T(p). \tag{7}
\]

We next prove the claimed affine list rather than assuming it in the endpoint notation.  Put
\[
\begin{array}{llll}
 A_1=\alpha_0,&A_2=\alpha_1,&A_3=1-\beta_0-\delta_1,&A_4=1-\delta_0-\beta_1,\\
 B_1=\beta_0,&B_2=\beta_1,&B_3=1-\alpha_0-\gamma_1,&B_4=1-\gamma_0-\alpha_1.
\end{array}
\]
Then \(u=\min_iA_i\), \(v=\min_jB_j\), and therefore
\[
 \kappa-(u+v)=\max_{1\le i,j\le4}\{\kappa-A_i-B_j\}. \tag{8}
\]
Direct substitution gives the following complete \(4\)-by-\(4\) array; every parenthesized remainder is nonpositive:
\[
\left(\kappa-A_i-B_j\right)_{i,j}=\begin{pmatrix}
\ell_1&\ell_2&\ell_3+(-1+\alpha_1+\beta_1+\gamma_1)&\ell_7\\
\ell_4&\ell_3&\ell_5&\ell_1+(-1+\alpha_0+\beta_0+\gamma_0)\\
\ell_3+(-1+\alpha_1+\beta_1+\delta_1)&\ell_8&\ell_3+(-2+\alpha_0+\alpha_1+\beta_0+\beta_1+\delta_1+\gamma_1)&\ell_2+(-2+\alpha_0+\alpha_1+\beta_0+\beta_1+\delta_1+\gamma_0)\\
\ell_6&\ell_1+(-1+\alpha_0+\beta_0+\delta_0)&\ell_4+(-2+\alpha_0+\alpha_1+\beta_0+\beta_1+\delta_0+\gamma_1)&\ell_1+(-2+\alpha_0+\alpha_1+\beta_0+\beta_1+\delta_0+\gamma_0)
\end{pmatrix}. \tag{9}
\]
For the four remainders with constant \(-1\), nonpositivity follows from arm normalization, for example
\[
 \alpha_1+\beta_1+\gamma_1\le1,\quad
 \alpha_0+\beta_0+\gamma_0\le1,\quad
 \alpha_1+\beta_1+\delta_1\le1,\quad
 \alpha_0+\beta_0+\delta_0\le1.
\]
For the four remainders with constant \(-2\), group their six probabilities by arm:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(\alpha_0+\beta_0)+(\alpha_1+\beta_1+\delta_1+\gamma_1)&\le2,\\
(\alpha_0+\beta_0+\gamma_0)+(\alpha_1+\beta_1+\delta_1)&\le2,\\
(\alpha_0+\beta_0+\delta_0)+(\alpha_1+\beta_1+\gamma_1)&\le2,\\
(\alpha_0+\beta_0+\delta_0+\gamma_0)+(\alpha_1+\beta_1)&\le2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus every entry in (9) is bounded above by one of \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_8\), while each of the eight \(\ell_j\)'s occurs as an equality entry.  Equations (8)--(9) prove
\[
 \kappa-(u+v)=\max_{1\le j\le8}\ell_j(p). \tag{10}
\]
For each trusted nuisance cell,
\[
 \kappa-h_{cy}=C^-_{c,y}(p).
\]
Since \(D_T(p)\) is the minimum of \(u+v\) and all the \(h_{cy}\)'s, (10) now yields
\[
 L_T(p)=\kappa-D_T(p)=\max_{f\in\mathfrak F^-_T}f(p). \tag{11}
\]
This is a complete evaluation list of eight base pieces and two labeled pieces for each \(c\in T\setminus\{a,b\}\); numerical coincidences on a boundary do not alter the list and no irredundancy assertion is needed.

Outcome reversal preserves compatibility because
\[
 \bar p^0_{xy}+\bar p^1_{x,1-y}=p^0_{x,1-y}+p^1_{xy}\le1.
\]
Complementing every bit of \(V\) and \(W\), while leaving \(X_0,X_1\) unchanged, is a bijection from \(\mathcal Q_T(p)\) to \(\mathcal Q_T(\bar p)\), and it sends the target to
\[
 \mathbb E[(1-V_b)-(1-V_a)]=-\theta_{ab}.
\]
Applying (7)--(11) to \(\bar p\), and then reversing the bits back, gives the finite upper witness \(q_T^+(p)\) and
\[
 \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)}\theta_{ab}(q)=-L_T(\bar p)=U_T(p)
 =\min_{f\in\mathfrak F^+_T}f(p). \tag{12}
\]
For every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), the mixture \(\lambda q_T^-(p)+(1-\lambda)q_T^+(p)\) remains compatible and has target \(\lambda L_T(p)+(1-\lambda)U_T(p)\).  Compactness and linearity together with (7) and (12) therefore prove the sharp equality
\[
 \Theta_I(P)=[L_T(p),U_T(p)].
\]
In particular, this is not merely an outer interval.  An affine lower inequality involving several nuisance categories cannot exceed \(L_T(p)\) at a compatible \(p\), because \(q_T^-(p)\) is a compatible counterexample to any larger lower value; the upper statement follows from \(q_T^+(p)\).  This proves the asserted absence of an additional mixed-category improvement.

Finally let \(T'=T\cup\{c\}\) and suppose \(p\) is \(T'\)-compatible.  The base eight pieces do not change and the only new lower pieces are \(C^-_{c,0},C^-_{c,1}\); outcome reversal gives the analogous upper statement.  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 L_{T'}(p)&=\max\{L_T(p),C^-_{c,0}(p),C^-_{c,1}(p)\},\\
 U_{T'}(p)&=\min\{U_T(p),C^+_{c,0}(p),C^+_{c,1}(p)\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Both changes are weak tightenings, and
\[
\{U_T-L_T\}-\{U_{T'}-L_{T'}\}
 =(L_{T'}-L_T)+(U_T-U_{T'})\ge0.
\]
It is strictly positive exactly when one summand is positive, which is precisely
\[
 \max_y C^-_{c,y}(p)>L_T(p)\quad\text{or}\quad
 \min_y C^+_{c,y}(p)<U_T(p).
\]
This also proves the strict-improvement criterion at ties.  Computing the eight base values and scanning the two lower and two upper values for each trusted nuisance category takes \(O(|\mathcal E|)\) arithmetic operations and simultaneously returns an active-face certificate.

If \(T=\{a,b\}\), the nuisance-cap collection is empty, so the definition of \(D_T\) gives \(D_T=u+v\).  Equation (10) in the sharp-envelope proof then gives
\[
 L_T(p)=\max_{1\le j\le8}\ell_j(p),\qquad
 U_T(p)=\min_{1\le j\le8}\{-\ell_j(\bar p)\}.
\]
Only \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\), the eight cells belonging to \(a\) and \(b\), occur.  Thus redistributing the remaining exposure probability among unrestricted categories changes none of these expressions.  Term-by-term, these are the Balke--Pearl binary-treatment risk-difference pieces, with the unrestricted residual exposure mass left unmodeled; this is the stated binary reduction \cite{BalkePearl1997ImperfectCompliance}.

If \(\mathcal E=\{a,b,c_\star\}\) and \(T=\mathcal E\), there is one trusted nuisance category.  The sharp-envelope theorem gives exactly the preceding eight lower pieces together with
\[
 C^-_{c_\star,y}(p)=\kappa-1+p^0_{c_\star y}+p^1_{c_\star,1-y},\qquad y\in\{0,1\},
\]
and gives their ten outcome-reversed negatives for the upper endpoint.  Direct relabeling of the two target exposure levels and the remaining level matches the ten lower and ten upper ternary expressions of Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjolander \cite{GabrielSachsSjolander2025Coarsening}.  Hence the ternary reduction is an algebraic specialization, not an appeal to a looser outer bound.

Finally, if \(T=\mathcal E\), then \(U=\varnothing\) and
\[
 \mathcal R_T=\mathcal E^2\times\{0,1\}^{\mathcal E},\qquad
 X=X_Z,\qquad Y=V_X.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal Q_T(p)\) is exactly the fully exclusion-valid finite categorical-IV response model: \(Z\) is randomized, \(X_z\) is the exposure response, and one common potential outcome \(V_x\) is used in both arms for every \(x\).  Projecting this model through the linear functional \(\mathbb E[V_b-V_a]\) is, by the sharp-envelope theorem, exactly \([L_T(p),U_T(p)]\).  This is the pairwise ATE projection of the arbitrary-finite categorical model characterized by Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson \cite{SongGuoChanRichardson2026CategoricalIV}.

Under \(q^{\rm sep}_{r,s,\tau,\lambda}\), the stipulated independence and the mixed-trust observation map give, for \(z\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
 p^{{\rm sep},z}_{a0}=A_z(1-\tau_a),&p^{{\rm sep},z}_{a1}=A_z\tau_a,\\
 p^{{\rm sep},z}_{b0}=B_z(1-\tau_b),&p^{{\rm sep},z}_{b1}=B_z\tau_b,
\end{array}
\]
and the four displayed \(c_\star\)-cell formulas.  These equalities are precisely the constraints defining \(\mathcal Q_{T_0}(p^{\rm sep})\), so the constructed response law belongs to that class.

The parameter ranges imply
\[
 1-r_z>\frac{8}{25},\qquad
 s_z,\ 1-s_z,\ \tau_x,\ 1-\tau_x>\frac25\quad(x=a,b).
\]
Consequently, every target-category observed cell is larger than
\[
 \frac{8}{25}\left(\frac25\right)^2=\frac{32}{625}>\frac{93}{5000}.
\]
For the two small nuisance cells,
\[
 r_0\lambda_0>\frac{31}{50}\frac{3}{100}=\frac{93}{5000},\qquad
 r_1(1-\lambda_1)>\frac{31}{50}\frac{3}{100}=\frac{93}{5000},
\]
and each of the other two nuisance cells is larger still because \(1-\lambda_0>93/100\) and \(\lambda_1>93/100\).  Hence every observed cell exceeds \(93/5000\).

Also
\[
 A_z<\frac{19}{50}\frac35=\frac{57}{250},\qquad
 B_z<\frac{19}{50}\frac35=\frac{57}{250}.
\]
Each target observed cell is bounded above by its category mass.  Therefore, for \(x\in\{a,b\}\) and \(y\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 p^{{\rm sep},0}_{xy}+p^{{\rm sep},1}_{x,1-y}<2\frac{57}{250}=\frac{57}{125}<1. \tag{13}
\]
This verifies \(T_0\)-compatibility directly as well as through the constructed law.  In contrast,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 p^{{\rm sep},0}_{c_\star0}+p^{{\rm sep},1}_{c_\star1}
 &=r_0(1-\lambda_0)+r_1\lambda_1\\
 &>2\frac{31}{50}\frac{93}{100}=\frac{2883}{2500}>1. \tag{14}
\end{aligned}
\]
The compatibility lemma says that (14) rules out every response law under \(T_1\).

Now let \(p'\) be armwise normalized and satisfy \(\|p'-p^{\rm sep}\|_\infty<1/200\).  Its smallest cell is greater than
\[
 \frac{93}{5000}-\frac1{200}=\frac{68}{5000}>0.
\]
Each left side of (13) increases by less than \(2/200=1/100\), and \(57/125+1/100<1\), so the compatibility lemma makes \(p'\) \(T_0\)-compatible.  On the other hand, (14) gives
\[
 p'^0_{c_\star0}+p'^1_{c_\star1}>\frac{2883}{2500}-\frac{2}{200}>1,
\]
so \(p'\) is not \(T_1\)-compatible.  This proves a positive-radius, full-dimensional obstruction inside the arm-normalization affine space.

For \(p^{\rm gain}\), both arm vectors sum to one and every cell is positive.  The compatibility sums for \(a\) and \(b\) all equal \(1/5\); those for \(c_\star\) are
\[
 p^{{\rm gain},0}_{c_\star0}+p^{{\rm gain},1}_{c_\star1}=\frac9{10},\qquad
 p^{{\rm gain},0}_{c_\star1}+p^{{\rm gain},1}_{c_\star0}=\frac3{10}.
\]
All defining inequalities are strict.  By the compatibility lemma, \(p^{\rm gain}\) is in the relative interior of the \(T_1\)-compatible polytope.

At this table,
\[
 \alpha_0=\alpha_1=\beta_0=\beta_1=\gamma_0=\gamma_1=\delta_0=\delta_1=\frac1{10},\qquad
 \kappa=-\frac35,\qquad u=v=\frac1{10}.
\]
Thus \(D_{T_0}=1/5\) and \(L_{T_0}=-4/5\).  The target cells are unchanged by outcome reversal, so \(U_{T_0}=4/5\).  Under \(T_1\),
\[
 h_{c_\star0}=1-\frac5{10}-\frac4{10}=\frac1{10},\qquad
 h_{c_\star1}=1-\frac1{10}-\frac2{10}=\frac7{10}.
\]
Hence \(D_{T_1}=1/10\) and \(L_{T_1}=-7/10\).  Outcome reversal interchanges these two nuisance caps, so \(U_{T_1}=7/10\).  The asserted strict inclusion follows.

An explicit stability radius is \(\eta_{\rm gain}=1/100\).  If \(p'\) is armwise normalized and \(\|p'-p^{\rm gain}\|_\infty<1/100\), then every cell exceeds \(9/100\).  The largest \(T_1\)-compatibility sum is less than \(9/10+2/100<1\), so \(p'\) remains \(T_1\)-compatible.  Moreover, all target cells lie in \((9/100,11/100)\), while the cross caps entering \(u\) and \(v\) exceed \(78/100\).  Therefore
\[
 \frac{18}{100}<D_{T_0}(p')<\frac{22}{100}.
\]
At the same time,
\[
 \frac8{100}<h_{c_\star0}(p')<\frac{12}{100},\qquad
 \frac{68}{100}<h_{c_\star1}(p')<\frac{72}{100},
\]
so \(D_{T_1}(p')=h_{c_\star0}(p')\) and
\[
 L_{T_1}(p')-L_{T_0}(p')=D_{T_0}(p')-D_{T_1}(p')>\frac6{100}. \tag{15}
\]
For \(\bar p'\), the same target-cell bounds hold and the small nuisance cap is \(h_{c_\star1}(\bar p')=h_{c_\star0}(p')\).  Thus the outcome-reversed version of (15) gives
\[
 U_{T_0}(p')-U_{T_1}(p')>\frac6{100}.
\]
The sharp-envelope theorem then proves the claimed perturbation-stable strict inclusion.

Fix realized assignments with \(N_0N_1>0\).  Under independent sampling, conditional on this assignment vector, the observations in arm \(z\) are independent draws from \(P(X,Y\mid Z=z)\), and the two arm collections are independent.  For a listed affine face \(f\), let
\[
 \mu_{fz}=\mathbb E_P[a_{fz}(X,Y)\mid Z=z].
\]
Its empirical error is
\[
 \widehat f-f(p)=\sum_{z=0}^1\frac1{N_z}\sum_{i:Z_i=z}\{a_{fz}(X_i,Y_i)-\mu_{fz}\}. \tag{16}
\]

We first give the bounded-variable exponential-moment argument used below.  If \(B\in[l,u]\), put \(R=u-l\).  For \(R>0\), normalize \(H=(B-l)/R\in[0,1]\) and write \(\mu=\mathbb E H\).  Convexity of the exponential gives \(e^{\lambda H}\le(1-H)+He^\lambda\), so
\[
 \log\mathbb E e^{\lambda(H-\mu)}\le g_\mu(\lambda)\equiv-\lambda\mu+\log(1-\mu+\mu e^\lambda).
\]
Here \(g_\mu(0)=g_\mu'(0)=0\), and, with \(w=\mu e^\lambda/(1-\mu+\mu e^\lambda)\),
\[
 g_\mu''(\lambda)=w(1-w)\le\frac14.
\]
Integrating this inequality twice from zero gives \(g_\mu(\lambda)\le\lambda^2/8\) for every real \(\lambda\).  Rescaling yields
\[
 \mathbb E e^{\lambda(B-\mathbb EB)}\le \exp\left(\frac{\lambda^2R^2}{8}\right). \tag{17}
\]
The case \(R=0\) is deterministic and satisfies (17) as well.  Multiplying (17) over independent summands and applying the exponential Markov inequality shows that, if their range lengths are \(R_k\),
\[
 \Pr\left\{\left|\sum_k(B_k-\mathbb EB_k)\right|\ge t\right\}\le
 2\exp\left\{-\frac{2t^2}{\sum_kR_k^2}\right\}, \tag{18}
\]
with the evident deterministic interpretation when the denominator is zero.  Indeed, the upper-tail exponent \(-\lambda t+\lambda^2\sum_kR_k^2/8\) is minimized at \(\lambda=4t/\sum_kR_k^2\), and the lower tail follows by replacing every summand by its negative.

In (16), each of the \(N_z\) arm-\(z\) summands has range length \(R_{fz}/N_z\).  Therefore (18) gives, conditionally on the assignment vector,
\[
 \Pr_P\{|\widehat f-f(p)|>\varepsilon_f\mid Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\}\le
 2\exp\left\{-\frac{2\varepsilon_f^2}{\sum_{z=0}^1R_{fz}^2/N_z}\right\}\le\frac{\alpha_{\rm conf}}{M_T}. \tag{19}
\]
When both ranges vanish, the face is constant and (19) holds with probability zero on the left.  A union bound over the \(M_T\) listed lower and upper faces gives the simultaneous event
\[
 \mathcal H=\bigcap_{f\in\mathfrak F^-_T\cup\mathfrak F^+_T}\{|\widehat f-f(p)|\le\varepsilon_f\},\qquad
 \Pr_P(\mathcal H\mid Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)\ge1-\alpha_{\rm conf}. \tag{20}
\]
The bound depends on the assignments only through \(N_0,N_1\).  Averaging (20) over assignment vectors conditional on these counts proves the same lower bound conditional on \((N_0,N_1)\).

On \(\mathcal H\), every lower face satisfies
\[
 f(\widehat p)-\varepsilon_f\le f(p)\le f(\widehat p)+\varepsilon_f.
\]
Taking maxima and using the sharp-envelope theorem yields
\[
 L_{\rm lo}\le\max_{f\in\mathfrak F^-_T}f(p)=L_T(p)\le L_{\rm hi}. \tag{21}
\]
Likewise, taking minima over the upper faces yields
\[
 U_{\rm lo}\le\min_{f\in\mathfrak F^+_T}f(p)=U_T(p)\le U_{\rm hi}. \tag{22}
\]
Equations (20)--(22) prove the conditional endpoint-rectangle coverage.  Because \(V_a,V_b\) are binary, \(-1\le L_T(p)\le U_T(p)\le1\).  Thus, on the same event,
\[
 [L_T(p),U_T(p)]\subseteq[L_{\rm lo},U_{\rm hi}]\cap[-1,1]=\mathcal C_{\rm set}. \tag{23}
\]

If an arm is empty, the stipulated endpoint box and \([-1,1]\) cover deterministically.  Hence, writing \(A=\{N_0N_1>0\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr_P\{\text{both coverages hold}\}
 &\ge \Pr_P(A)(1-\alpha_{\rm conf})+\Pr_P(A^c)\\
 &=1-\alpha_{\rm conf}\Pr_P(A)\ge1-\alpha_{\rm conf}.
\end{aligned}
\]
No step divides by a cell probability, selects an active face, or requires a strict face gap.  Zero cells and affine-face ties therefore cause no exception; a zero-range face was handled explicitly after (19).  This proves the asserted finite-sample whole-set result on every compatible observed law.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every wholly untrusted refinement \(g:\widetilde{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal E\), the refined table \(\widetilde p\) is \(\widetilde T\)-compatible if and only if its push-forward \(p\) is \(T\)-compatible.  Whenever these equivalent conditions hold,
\[
 L_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)=L_T(p),\qquad
 U_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)=U_T(p),
\]
and hence the two sharp identified intervals are equal.  Thus splitting or merging bins wholly inside the untrusted part is exactly target-ancillary.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By the definition of a wholly untrusted refinement, every trusted category \(x\in T\) has one refined preimage \(\widetilde x\in\widetilde T\).  The armwise push-forward equations therefore reduce on that category to
\[
 \widetilde p^z_{\widetilde x y}=p^z_{xy},\qquad z,y\in\{0,1\}.
\]
All other refined children lie over \(U\) and are untrusted.  The compatibility inequalities in the compatibility lemma consequently correspond one-to-one:
\[
 \widetilde p^0_{\widetilde x y}+\widetilde p^1_{\widetilde x,1-y}\le1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 p^0_{xy}+p^1_{x,1-y}\le1,\qquad x\in T.
\]
Normalization is preserved by push-forward, so compatibility is equivalent.

The unique refined preimages of the two target categories have exactly the same \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\) values as the coarse table.  Hence \(\kappa,u,v\) agree.  Each trusted nuisance category also has a unique preimage with identical two arm cells, so its two \(h\)-values agree; no child of an untrusted category contributes an \(h\)-value.  Therefore
\[
 D_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)=D_T(p),\qquad
 D_{\widetilde T}(\overline{\widetilde p})=D_T(\bar p).
\]
The endpoint formulas give the two asserted equalities, and the sharp-envelope theorem turns them into equality of the identified intervals.  A split is represented by \(g\), while a merge is the reverse comparison under the same push-forward, so both operations are covered.

added_lemmas.statement: For fixed target categories \(a,b\), both sharp endpoints and an active-face certificate can be evaluated with a number of arithmetic operations linear in \(|\mathcal E|\): evaluate the eight base lower pieces and their eight outcome-reversed negatives once, scan the two lower and two upper pieces for each \(c\in T\setminus\{a,b\}\), and retain the maximizing lower and minimizing upper labels.  One active label per endpoint uses constant working storage; reporting every tied label uses storage proportional to the output size.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The sharp-envelope theorem identifies \(L_T(p)\) with the maximum over \(8+2|T\setminus\{a,b\}|\) explicitly affine values and \(U_T(p)\) with the minimum over the same number of outcome-reversed values.  Each value uses a bounded number of additions and comparisons after the target-cell quantities and \(\kappa\) are computed.  The number of face evaluations satisfies
\[
 8+2|T\setminus\{a,b\}|\le 2|\mathcal E|+8,
\]
so a running maximum and minimum require linearly many operations and constant working storage.  Retaining the label whenever a strict improvement occurs returns one active face.  Appending rather than discarding labels at equality reports all ties and uses only storage proportional to the number of reported labels.

open_obligations.what_is_open: An explicit calibration and proof for one multiplier rectangle that is uniformly valid across simultaneous local face ties and vanishing face variances, while also strictly improving expected total width on every compact regular class.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen handle does not specify the near-active threshold, the variance-degeneracy threshold, or the multiplier critical-value rule. A regular finite-dimensional Gaussian approximation does not control triangular arrays at the transition where variances vanish and the data-dependent splice can select the Gaussian branch with nonnegligible probability.
open_obligations.attempted: Conditioning on the finite face vector, self-normalized near-active selection, and a variance-threshold fallback reduce the issue to uniform control of selection error and Gaussian anti-concentration near the threshold. The stated primitives supply neither that transition theorem nor enough calibration detail to derive it without assuming the crux.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The proved finite-sample fallback satisfies, for every sample size \(n\) and every compatible \(P\),
\[
 \Pr_P\!\left\{(L_T(p),U_T(p))\in\mathcal C_{\rm end},\ [L_T(p),U_T(p)]\subseteq\mathcal C_{\rm set}\right\}\ge1-\alpha_{\rm conf},
\]
including local or exact face ties, zero cells, vanishing face variances, and empty instrument arms under the stipulated trivial output.  This establishes the unrestricted validity rung, but it does not establish the strict regular-class expected-width ratio for the proposed Gaussian rectangle.
